---
title: "Inspection games (deterrence & monitoring)"
toc: true
---

## What it is
Inspection games model strategic interaction between:
- an agent who may violate (offend), and
- an enforcer who can monitor/inspect at a cost.

They are used to formalize deterrence when enforcement resources are scarce.

---

## Canonical setup
Offender chooses $C$ (crime) or $N$ (no crime).  
Enforcer chooses $I$ (inspect) or $\bar I$ (not inspect).

Parameters:
- offender benefit if successful: $b>0$
- sanction if caught: $s>0$
- harm to enforcer if crime succeeds: $h>0$
- inspection cost to enforcer: $k>0$

Payoffs:
- If $N$: offender $0$; enforcer gets $-k$ if inspecting, $0$ otherwise.
- If $C$ and $I$: offender caught $\to -s$; enforcer pays inspection cost $\to -k$.
- If $C$ and $\bar I$: offender succeeds $\to b$; enforcer suffers harm $\to -h$.

---

## Solved equilibrium (mixed strategies)
Let enforcer inspect with probability $q$. Let offender commit crime with probability $p$.

### Step 1: offender indifference
Expected payoff from crime:
$$
\mathbb{E}[u_O(C)] = q(-s) + (1-q)b = b - q(b+s).
$$
Indifference with $N$ (payoff 0) gives:
$$
b - q(b+s)=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad q^*=\frac{b}{b+s}.
$$

### Step 2: enforcer indifference
Enforcer payoff from inspecting:
$$
\mathbb{E}[u_E(I)] = -k
$$
(since inspection cost is paid regardless of offender action)

Enforcer payoff from not inspecting:
$$
\mathbb{E}[u_E(\bar I)] = -ph.
$$
Indifference gives:
$$
-k=-ph \quad\Rightarrow\quad p^*=\frac{k}{h}.
$$

### Conditions
A true interior mixed equilibrium requires $0<p^*<1$, i.e.:
$$
0<\frac{k}{h}<1 \quad \Leftrightarrow \quad 0<k<h.
$$

---

## Comparative statics (predictions)
- Higher sanctions $s$ reduce the inspection probability needed for deterrence:
  $q^*=\frac{b}{b+s}$ decreases in $s$.
- Higher illegal gain $b$ increases required inspection intensity.
- Higher inspection cost $k$ increases crime probability $p^*=k/h$.
- Higher harm $h$ decreases crime probability (enforcement becomes more willing to deter).

---

## Interpretation and links
- This is the cleanest “deterrence as equilibrium” baseline.
- Extensions:
  - multiple crime types (substitution),
  - heterogeneous offenders (concentration),
  - reporting stage (endogenous detection),
  - dynamic enforcement with learning.
